chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook
chunks.snippet:
**Northstar Technologies | Policy HR-001 | Version 1.0**

> **Fictional training document.** Northstar Technologies, its contacts, portals, and policies are invented for RAG demonstration. This handbook is not legal advice or an employment contract.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 1. Purpose and scope > 1.1 Purpose
chunks.snippet: This handbook introduces Northstar Technologies' workplace expectations, employee resources, and procedures. It is intended as a starting point, not a replacement for the topic-specific policies listed in Section 13. Employees should consult the applicable detailed policy when a question concerns a specific entitlement, deadline, approval, or exception.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 1. Purpose and scope > 1.2 Who is covered
chunks.snippet: Unless a section says otherwise, this handbook applies to Northstar's US-based employees, whether working at an office, remotely, or on an approved hybrid schedule. Contractors, consultants, and agency workers follow their agreements and applicable site/security rules; they do not automatically receive employee benefits or PTO.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 1. Purpose and scope > 1.3 Policy precedence
chunks.snippet: Applicable law and signed agreements take precedence over this handbook where required. A topic-specific policy controls over a general handbook summary. People Operations resolves apparent inconsistencies and publishes clarifications; managers cannot unilaterally waive written policies. State and local requirements may provide greater protections or benefits.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 1. Purpose and scope > 1.4 No guarantee of employment
chunks.snippet: This handbook does not create a contract or guarantee continued employment. Where lawful, employment is at will, meaning either Northstar or the employee may end employment at any time, subject to applicable law and agreements.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 2. Company overview > 2.1 Our business
chunks.snippet: Northstar Technologies develops workflow and analytics software for small and mid-sized businesses. Its headquarters is in Denver, Colorado, and it employs approximately 250 people across engineering, product, customer success, sales, finance, operations, and corporate functions.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 2. Company overview > 2.2 Our values
chunks.snippet:
- **Customer clarity:** Explain decisions and commitments in plain language.
- **Ownership:** Take responsibility for outcomes, not just tasks.
- **Security by default:** Protect customer and employee information.
- **Respect:** Treat colleagues and customers professionally.
- **Continuous improvement:** Raise concerns and improve processes without blame.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 2. Company overview > 2.3 Working language and communications
chunks.snippet: English is the primary language for company-wide documentation and meetings. Employees should use accessible, respectful language and summarize decisions in the appropriate team workspace. Confidential information must be shared only in approved systems with authorized recipients.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 3. Employment categories and records > 3.1 Employment classifications
chunks.snippet: Employees are designated full-time or part-time and exempt or nonexempt under applicable wage-and-hour rules. Full-time generally means a regularly scheduled 40-hour workweek; part-time means fewer than 30 scheduled hours per week. Schedules between 30 and 39 hours are evaluated individually by People Operations for benefits eligibility. Exempt/nonexempt classification determines overtime and timekeeping requirements; it does not alone determine PTO eligibility.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 3. Employment categories and records > 3.2 Employee records
chunks.snippet: Employees must keep their legal name, mailing address, emergency contact, tax withholding, and direct deposit information current in the fictional **Northstar People Portal**. Report changes within five business days when practical. Access to personnel files is limited to authorized staff with a legitimate business need.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 3. Employment categories and records > 3.3 Probationary periods
chunks.snippet: Northstar does not impose a universal probationary period. Managers conduct structured check-ins during the first 30, 60, and 90 days; these check-ins do not change employment status or statutory rights.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 3. Employment categories and records > 3.4 Employment verification
chunks.snippet: Direct employment-verification requests to People Operations. Managers should not independently disclose salary, performance, or personnel information to third parties.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 4. Work schedules and attendance > 4.1 Standard hours
chunks.snippet: Most corporate teams coordinate around **9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Mountain Time, Monday through Friday**, with reasonable flexibility for time zones and role requirements. The standard full-time schedule is 40 working hours per week, with meal and rest breaks handled according to applicable law. Team coverage hours may differ for customer-facing functions.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 4. Work schedules and attendance > 4.2 Attendance and availability
chunks.snippet: Employees are expected to attend required meetings, meet agreed deadlines, maintain accurate calendar availability, and notify their manager as soon as possible when an unexpected absence affects work. Employees should not work while on approved PTO except in exceptional circumstances coordinated through People Operations.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 4. Work schedules and attendance > 4.3 Timekeeping and overtime
chunks.snippet: Nonexempt employees must record all hours worked in the People Portal daily, including work performed remotely. Off-the-clock work is prohibited. Obtain manager approval before planned overtime; all hours actually worked must still be reported and paid as required by law. Exempt employees should record absences as directed but do not submit hourly timecards unless instructed.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 4. Work schedules and attendance > 4.4 Breaks
chunks.snippet: Employees should take required meal and rest breaks. Specific duration and timing follow the law of the employee's work location. Questions about local requirements go to People Operations.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 5. Workplace locations and remote work > 5.1 Hybrid and remote arrangements
chunks.snippet: Some roles are office-based, hybrid, or fully remote. A manager and People Operations must approve a permanent change in work arrangement. Hybrid employees ordinarily attend their assigned office on **Tuesday and Thursday**, unless their team's approved schedule differs. Working from another state or country requires prior written approval because of tax, security, employment, and customer-contract considerations.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 5. Workplace locations and remote work > 5.2 Remote-work standards
chunks.snippet: Employees working remotely must maintain a safe, reasonably private workspace, a reliable internet connection, and availability during agreed collaboration hours. Work-related records must remain in company-approved systems; employees may not use shared household accounts or devices for company work.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 5. Workplace locations and remote work > 5.3 Office access and visitors
chunks.snippet: Employees must use their assigned badge and must not lend it to others. Register visitors in advance, escort them in restricted areas, and report lost badges to Facilities and IT promptly. Follow posted emergency and building instructions.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 5. Workplace locations and remote work > 5.4 Detailed rules
chunks.snippet: See **HR-004 Remote Work Policy** for eligibility, location approvals, equipment, and exceptions. See **IT-001 Equipment Policy** and **SEC-001 Data Security Policy** for device and information controls.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 6. Compensation, payroll, and performance > 6.1 Payroll
chunks.snippet: Employees are paid **semi-monthly on the 15th and last calendar day of each month**, or the preceding business day when a pay date falls on a weekend or company holiday. Payroll statements are available in the People Portal. Report suspected errors to Payroll within five business days of discovery; the company will investigate and correct errors as required by law.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 6. Compensation, payroll, and performance > 6.2 Pay changes and bonuses
chunks.snippet: Compensation adjustments and incentive awards require documented approval under the applicable compensation plan. Verbal statements do not override signed offer letters or approved plans.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 6. Compensation, payroll, and performance > 6.3 Performance conversations
chunks.snippet: Managers hold quarterly development conversations and an annual performance review. Reviews cover results, collaboration, professional growth, and compliance with company expectations. Employees may request clarification or submit a written response through People Operations.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 6. Compensation, payroll, and performance > 6.4 Professional development
chunks.snippet: Role-related learning may be supported when budgeted and approved in advance. Training expenses follow **FIN-001 Expense Reimbursement Policy**; participation in optional training does not automatically qualify for reimbursement.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 7. Paid time off, holidays, and leave > 7.1 PTO overview
chunks.snippet:
Eligible regular full-time employees receive annual PTO based on tenure: **15 days (120 hours)** for fewer than three completed years of service and **20 days (160 hours)** beginning on the third service anniversary. PTO is tracked in hours and accrued each semi-monthly pay period. Requests normally require at least five business days' notice and manager approval. Carryover is capped at **five days (40 hours)**, subject to applicable law.

**Authoritative source:** **HR-002 Paid Time Off Policy** contains eligibility, accrual calculations, new-hire rules, request timing, balance limits, carryover, separation treatment, and examples. Where a summary here differs from HR-002, consult HR-002 and People Operations.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 7. Paid time off, holidays, and leave > 7.2 Company holidays
chunks.snippet: Northstar observes designated paid company holidays and publishes the annual calendar before the start of each year. Holiday pay and floating-holiday eligibility are addressed in **HR-003 Holiday Policy**. A holiday is not automatically deducted from an employee's PTO balance.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 7. Paid time off, holidays, and leave > 7.3 Other leave
chunks.snippet: Medical, family, parental, bereavement, jury-duty, military, and other protected or company-provided leaves may have separate eligibility and documentation rules. Contact People Operations rather than assuming PTO is required. See **HR-006 Leave of Absence Policy**.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 7. Paid time off, holidays, and leave > 7.4 Reporting unexpected absences
chunks.snippet: Notify your manager as soon as reasonably possible using an approved channel, preferably before your scheduled start. For an absence that may qualify as protected leave, contact People Operations; employees should not disclose detailed medical information to a manager unnecessarily.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 8. Benefits and employee support > 8.1 Benefits overview
chunks.snippet: Northstar offers eligible employees a benefits package that may include medical, dental, and vision coverage; a retirement savings plan; life and disability insurance; and an employee assistance program. Specific eligibility, premiums, enrollment windows, and plan terms are in **BEN-001 Employee Benefits Guide** and the governing plan documents.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 8. Benefits and employee support > 8.2 Enrollment and changes
chunks.snippet: New hires receive benefits enrollment instructions during onboarding. Employees should report qualifying life events promptly through the People Portal. Benefit elections and deadlines are governed by the plan and applicable law, not informal statements from a manager.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 8. Benefits and employee support > 8.3 Confidential support
chunks.snippet: Employees can contact People Operations privately about benefits access, workplace accommodations, and available support. Sensitive health information is handled with restricted access.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 9. Expenses, travel, and purchasing > 9.1 Business expenses
chunks.snippet: Reasonable, necessary business expenses may be reimbursed when documented and approved under **FIN-001 Expense Reimbursement Policy**. Employees should seek preapproval for travel and purchases when required; a manager's verbal encouragement does not replace the expense workflow.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 9. Expenses, travel, and purchasing > 9.2 Receipts and submissions
chunks.snippet: Submit itemized receipts and a clear business purpose through the fictional **Northstar Expense Portal**. Personal purchases, duplicate claims, and unsupported expenses may be denied, subject to legal reimbursement requirements.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 9. Expenses, travel, and purchasing > 9.3 Corporate cards
chunks.snippet: Company cards are for authorized business use only. Lost cards and suspicious charges must be reported immediately to Finance. Do not share card details or store them in unapproved applications.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 10. Information security and technology > 10.1 Acceptable use
chunks.snippet: Use approved company accounts, devices, and collaboration tools for company work. Do not install unapproved software, disable endpoint protection, or transfer confidential data to personal cloud storage or personal email.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 10. Information security and technology > 10.2 Authentication and access
chunks.snippet: Multi-factor authentication is required on supported company systems. Employees must use unique credentials and an approved password manager, never share passwords, and promptly report suspected account compromise. Access is granted according to job responsibilities and removed when no longer needed.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 10. Information security and technology > 10.3 Reporting incidents
chunks.snippet: Report suspected phishing, lost devices, unintended disclosures, or unusual account activity **immediately** through the fictional **IT Service Desk** or to `security@northstar.example`. Do not investigate suspected breaches independently or delete relevant evidence. **SEC-001 Data Security Policy** specifies incident response steps.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 10. Information security and technology > 10.4 AI tools and confidential information
chunks.snippet: Do not enter confidential customer data, source code, credentials, personnel information, or nonpublic financial data into unapproved external AI tools. Approved tools and permissible data categories are listed in SEC-001; ask Security when uncertain.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 11. Workplace conduct and reporting > 11.1 Respectful workplace
chunks.snippet: Northstar expects respectful interactions, fair treatment, and professional behavior in offices, online meetings, messaging platforms, and company-sponsored events. Harassment, discrimination, bullying, threats, and retaliation are prohibited.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 11. Workplace conduct and reporting > 11.2 Conflicts of interest
chunks.snippet: Employees must disclose outside work, financial interests, gifts, or relationships that could compromise—or appear to compromise—objective business judgment. Disclosures go to People Operations or Legal for review.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 11. Workplace conduct and reporting > 11.3 Reporting concerns
chunks.snippet: Employees may report workplace concerns to their manager, People Operations, or the fictional confidential channel `ethics@northstar.example`. Employees may bypass their manager, especially if the manager is involved. Northstar prohibits retaliation for good-faith reporting or participation in an investigation.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 11. Workplace conduct and reporting > 11.4 Investigations and confidentiality
chunks.snippet: Reports are reviewed promptly and shared only with those who need information to assess and respond. Absolute confidentiality cannot be promised. Employees are expected to cooperate honestly; corrective action depends on the findings and circumstances. See **HR-007 Workplace Conduct Policy**.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 12. Joining, changing roles, and leaving > 12.1 Onboarding
chunks.snippet: New hires complete identity and employment paperwork, required security training, benefits enrollment, and role-specific orientation. Managers arrange initial access and equipment using **HR-005 Onboarding Procedures**.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 12. Joining, changing roles, and leaving > 12.2 Internal transfers
chunks.snippet: Employees interested in an internal role should review eligibility and discuss timing with People Operations. System permissions and equipment needs must be reassessed when responsibilities change.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 12. Joining, changing roles, and leaving > 12.3 Departures
chunks.snippet: Employees should notify their manager and People Operations in writing when resigning. The company coordinates final pay, benefits notices, system access removal, and equipment return in accordance with applicable law. PTO payout is governed by **HR-002** and applicable state/local requirements.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 12. Joining, changing roles, and leaving > 12.4 Return of company property
chunks.snippet: Return laptops, badges, keys, cards, and other company property using the process supplied by IT. Do not erase or retain company records on personal accounts or storage devices.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 14. Frequently asked questions > 14.1 Can I work from another state for two weeks?
chunks.snippet: Not without prior written approval. Submit the proposed dates and location to your manager and People Operations; see HR-004.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 14. Frequently asked questions > 14.2 Do I need to use PTO for a company holiday?
chunks.snippet: Ordinarily no. Paid holidays are tracked separately. Check HR-003 for eligibility and schedule exceptions.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 14. Frequently asked questions > 14.3 Who approves my vacation request?
chunks.snippet: Your manager approves scheduling requests through the People Portal; People Operations administers balances and exceptions. See HR-002.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 14. Frequently asked questions > 14.4 What if I click a suspicious link?
chunks.snippet: Report it immediately to the IT Service Desk or Security, even if you are unsure whether data was exposed. See SEC-001.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 14. Frequently asked questions > 14.5 Can I expense a new home-office monitor?
chunks.snippet: Do not assume reimbursement. Obtain approval under IT-001 and FIN-001 before purchasing.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 14. Frequently asked questions > 14.6 Can my manager change my PTO accrual rate?
chunks.snippet: No. PTO accrual follows HR-002 and applicable law. People Operations reviews eligibility and corrections.

chunks.title: Employee Handbook
chunks.section: Employee Handbook > 15. Document governance
chunks.snippet: People Operations owns this handbook and reviews it annually and after material policy or legal changes. The current approved version is the one published in the internal policy repository. Archived copies should be marked superseded and excluded from the active RAG knowledge base. Questions about interpretation should be escalated to People Operations rather than answered from outdated excerpts.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.snippet:
**Northstar Technologies | Policy HR-002 | Version 1.0**

> **Fictional training document.** This policy is invented for RAG evaluation and does not establish actual legal entitlements. Applicable state and local law overrides a conflicting rule, including rules on accrual, carryover, paid sick leave, and payout.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 1. Purpose and authority > 1.1 Purpose
chunks.snippet: Northstar provides paid time off (PTO) so eligible employees can rest, attend to personal needs, and take planned time away from work. This policy defines eligibility, accrual, scheduling, carryover, and separation treatment.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 1. Purpose and authority > 1.2 Relationship to other policies
chunks.snippet: **HR-001 Employee Handbook** provides general workplace context. **HR-003 Holiday Policy** covers paid holidays and floating holidays. **HR-006 Leave of Absence Policy** covers protected and extended leave. PTO is not a substitute for statutory leave rights, and a holiday is not automatically charged to PTO.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 1. Purpose and authority > 1.3 Authority and exceptions
chunks.snippet: People Operations administers balances and interprets this policy. Managers approve time away based on staffing but cannot change accrual rates, waive legal requirements, or promise extra PTO. Exceptions require written approval from People Operations and must comply with applicable law.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 2. Eligibility > 2.1 Eligible employees
chunks.snippet: Regular US-based full-time employees scheduled for **40 hours per week** are eligible for PTO starting on their first day of employment. Employees regularly scheduled for **30–39 hours** are evaluated by People Operations and, if designated PTO-eligible, receive a prorated allowance based on their standard scheduled hours divided by 40. This designation is recorded in the People Portal.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 2. Eligibility > 2.2 Employees not covered by this plan
chunks.snippet: Regular part-time employees scheduled for fewer than 30 hours, interns, contractors, and temporary agency workers do not participate in this company PTO plan unless their written agreement or applicable law requires otherwise. They may still have separate paid-sick-leave or other statutory entitlements; contact People Operations for the rules in their work location.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 2. Eligibility > 2.3 New hires and service dates
chunks.snippet: PTO begins accruing on the hire date. An employee's service anniversary is the same month and day as the hire date; People Operations adjusts leap-day anniversaries to February 28 in non-leap years for this plan. Prior contractor service does not count toward the PTO tenure tier unless People Operations documents an exception.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 3. Annual allowance and accrual > 3.1 Full-time PTO tiers
chunks.snippet:
| Completed service | Annual PTO allowance | Equivalent hours |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Less than 3 years | 15 workdays | 120 hours |
| 3 years or more | 20 workdays | 160 hours |

A workday means eight hours for a standard 40-hour, five-day schedule. PTO balances and requests are recorded in **hours**, not fractions of calendar days.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 3. Annual allowance and accrual > 3.2 Semi-monthly accrual
chunks.snippet:
Northstar has **24 semi-monthly payroll periods** per calendar year. For an employee eligible for a full year at the same tier and schedule, the standard credit is:

- 120 hours / 24 = **5.0000 hours per payroll period** for the 15-day tier.
- 160 hours / 24 = **6.6667 hours per payroll period** for the 20-day tier, with an annual true-up so total regular annual accrual is exactly 160 hours.

Credits post at the close of each pay period, subject to any lawful balance cap. The People Portal displays balances to two decimal places; Payroll maintains greater internal precision and adjusts the final annual posting to prevent rounding drift.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 3. Annual allowance and accrual > 3.3 Partial periods and midyear changes
chunks.snippet: For a new hire, separation, or schedule change within a pay period, the credit is prorated by **eligible calendar days in that pay period divided by total calendar days in that pay period**. A tenure-tier change on the third anniversary is calculated separately for the days before and after the anniversary. People Operations handles these adjustments in the People Portal.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 3. Annual allowance and accrual > 3.4 Prorated schedules
chunks.snippet: An approved PTO-eligible employee scheduled for 32 hours per week receives 32/40 = **80%** of the full-time annual hours: 96 hours at the lower tier or 128 hours at the higher tier for a complete year. PTO requests reflect the hours the employee was otherwise scheduled to work.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 3. Annual allowance and accrual > 3.5 Balance cap
chunks.snippet: The normal PTO balance cap is **200 hours** for a full-time employee; for a prorated eligible schedule, the cap is scaled by the same scheduled-hours ratio. Accrual pauses when the balance reaches the cap and resumes when the balance falls below it. Northstar will apply any more protective accrual or cap rule required by law. Accrual not posted because of a lawful cap is not retroactively credited.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 4. Using PTO > 4.1 Permitted uses
chunks.snippet: PTO may be used for vacations, personal appointments, family responsibilities, rest, and other personal needs. Employees do not need to provide private details for ordinary PTO requests. When an absence may qualify for protected leave or legally required sick time, People Operations will help identify the applicable policy and legal rights.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 4. Using PTO > 4.2 Request increments
chunks.snippet: Employees may request PTO in **one-hour increments**, or smaller increments where required by law or an approved accommodation. An employee should request only the hours they would otherwise have worked.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 4. Using PTO > 4.3 Advance notice
chunks.snippet: For planned absences, submit a request in the **Northstar People Portal at least five business days before the first day off**. A business day means Monday through Friday excluding Northstar company holidays. For an absence longer than five consecutive workdays, employees are encouraged to give at least 20 business days' notice, but this is a planning recommendation, not an additional mandatory minimum.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 4. Using PTO > 4.4 Approval workflow
chunks.snippet:
1. Employee checks the projected PTO balance and team calendar.
2. Employee submits dates, hours, and optional coverage notes in the People Portal.
3. The system routes the request to the direct manager.
4. The manager approves or denies based on coverage, workload, and equitable scheduling, normally within **three business days**.
5. The portal notifies the employee and updates the projected balance. Actual PTO is deducted when the absence is processed.

A submitted request is **not approved** until the portal shows an approved status. Managers should explain denials and work with employees on alternatives. Approval must not interfere with legally protected leave.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 4. Using PTO > 4.5 Competing requests and peak periods
chunks.snippet: Managers consider business coverage, prior commitments, fairness, and the order requests were received. No team has an automatic company-wide blackout period. A team proposing a temporary coverage restriction must obtain People Operations review and communicate it in advance; legally protected absences remain protected.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 4. Using PTO > 4.6 Unexpected absences
chunks.snippet: Notify your manager as soon as reasonably possible, preferably before your shift starts. Enter the absence in the People Portal when able. Do not delay reporting a protected or urgent absence to meet the five-business-day planned-request rule. People Operations may route the absence under HR-006 or a legally required sick-leave process.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 5. Balances, borrowing, and changes > 5.1 Available versus projected balance
chunks.snippet: **Available balance** is accrued unused PTO as of the latest processed payroll period. **Projected balance** includes expected future accrual through the requested date and subtracts approved future PTO. A projected balance is an estimate, not a guarantee.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 5. Balances, borrowing, and changes > 5.2 Negative balances
chunks.snippet: PTO may not ordinarily be used before it is accrued. A manager cannot approve a negative balance. People Operations may approve a documented exception of up to **16 hours** of advanced PTO for an eligible employee after reviewing the circumstances; repayment or final-pay deductions are permitted only where lawful and separately authorized when required.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 5. Balances, borrowing, and changes > 5.3 Cancelling or changing PTO
chunks.snippet: Employees may cancel or edit future approved requests in the People Portal. Changes to dates or hours are routed back to the manager for approval. If plans change after an absence begins, notify the manager and People Operations promptly so records can be corrected.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 5. Balances, borrowing, and changes > 5.4 Holidays during PTO
chunks.snippet: If an eligible employee's approved PTO overlaps an observed paid company holiday, the holiday is generally recorded as holiday pay rather than PTO for the employee's normally scheduled hours. See HR-003 for eligibility and observed dates. Example: a five-day vacation containing one eight-hour paid holiday ordinarily uses **32 PTO hours**, not 40.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 6. Year-end carryover and forfeiture > 6.1 Standard carryover rule
chunks.snippet: At the transition from December 31 to January 1, employees may carry over up to **40 unused PTO hours (five standard workdays)**. Under the fictional default company plan, unused hours above 40 expire after year-end processing **only where lawful**. In jurisdictions where accrued vacation cannot lawfully be forfeited, People Operations applies the required alternative and documents it in the employee's local policy addendum.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 6. Year-end carryover and forfeiture > 6.2 Carryover and new-year accrual
chunks.snippet: Carried hours remain part of the employee's PTO balance and count toward the 200-hour normal balance cap. New-year accrual posts on the usual payroll schedule; carryover is not a separate annual grant.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 6. Year-end carryover and forfeiture > 6.3 Example: year-end balance
chunks.snippet: An employee has 56 unused PTO hours on December 31. Under the default rule, **40 hours carry into January** and **16 hours expire**, provided the employee's jurisdiction permits forfeiture. In a jurisdiction prohibiting forfeiture, the local legal rule controls and the 16 hours must not simply be removed.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 6. Year-end carryover and forfeiture > 6.4 No cash-out election
chunks.snippet: Employees cannot elect to exchange unused PTO for cash while actively employed under the standard plan. Mandatory payments required by law or a written approved agreement are exceptions.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 7. Leave interactions and special situations > 7.1 Paid holidays
chunks.snippet: Company holidays are separate from PTO and governed by HR-003. An employee who is ineligible for holiday pay should ask People Operations how the day is recorded rather than assume it is automatically PTO.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 7. Leave interactions and special situations > 7.2 Protected leave and sick time
chunks.snippet: Medical, family, parental, disability-related, military, and other protected absences may have distinct eligibility, job-protection, notice, and pay rules. People Operations determines whether PTO may or must run concurrently with a leave, consistent with applicable law. Employees are not required to disclose diagnoses to their manager to request ordinary PTO.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 7. Leave interactions and special situations > 7.3 Accrual during leave
chunks.snippet: PTO accrues during paid working time and paid PTO under the standard plan. During an **unpaid leave**, PTO accrual is generally suspended for the unpaid days, unless applicable law or a written leave arrangement requires otherwise. People Operations calculates prorated pay-period credits when a leave begins or ends midperiod.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 7. Leave interactions and special situations > 7.4 Company closures
chunks.snippet: A scheduled company holiday follows HR-003. For an unscheduled office closure, People Operations and Payroll communicate whether affected employees are paid, work remotely, or use another approved status. Employees should not self-charge PTO without instructions.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 8. Separation and payout > 8.1 Final balance reconciliation
chunks.snippet: On separation, People Operations reconciles accrued hours, PTO used, approved adjustments, and local-law requirements through the final date of employment. Future projected accrual after separation is not earned.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 8. Separation and payout > 8.2 Unused PTO payout
chunks.snippet: **Unused accrued PTO is paid out at separation where required by applicable law or a written agreement.** Under the fictional default plan, there is no discretionary payout in jurisdictions that do not require it. People Operations must review the employee's work location before finalizing any payout; managers must not promise that PTO will or will not be paid.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 8. Separation and payout > 8.3 Negative balances at separation
chunks.snippet: If an employee has an authorized advanced-PTO deficit, Payroll may recover it only when permitted by applicable law and any required written authorization. Otherwise Northstar absorbs the deficit.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 8. Separation and payout > 8.4 PTO during notice periods
chunks.snippet: Employees may request PTO during a resignation notice period, but approval depends on operational coverage and legal obligations. PTO does not automatically extend the employment end date. Protected leave rights remain unaffected.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 9. Roles, records, and escalation
chunks.snippet:
| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Employee | Submit accurate requests, check balances, communicate absences |
| Manager | Review requests promptly and fairly, coordinate coverage |
| People Operations | Determine eligibility, administer exceptions, interpret local rules |
| Payroll | Post accruals, reconcile balances, process lawful final payments |

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 9. Roles, records, and escalation > 9.1 Record corrections
chunks.snippet: If an employee believes a PTO balance is incorrect, they should email `people@northstar.example` with the pay period, dates, and discrepancy. People Operations acknowledges the inquiry within **two business days** and aims to resolve straightforward corrections within **ten business days**. Complex local-law questions may take longer; the employee will receive an update.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 9. Roles, records, and escalation > 9.2 Appeals of scheduling decisions
chunks.snippet: An employee who disagrees with a denied PTO request should first discuss alternatives with the manager. If the employee believes the decision is inconsistent, discriminatory, retaliatory, or contrary to protected leave rights, they may contact People Operations directly or report through `ethics@northstar.example`.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 9. Roles, records, and escalation > 9.3 Data handling
chunks.snippet: PTO balances and absence reasons are personnel data. Managers should access only information needed for scheduling. Medical documentation, if needed for another leave process, must be sent to People Operations through approved secure channels, not posted in team chats.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 10. Worked examples > 10.1 Employee with two years of service
chunks.snippet:
**Question:** How much PTO does a full-time employee receive after two years?  
**Answer:** 120 hours (15 eight-hour days) annually, accruing at 5 hours per semi-monthly payroll period for a complete year at the lower tier.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 10. Worked examples > 10.2 Third service anniversary
chunks.snippet:
**Question:** What happens when an employee reaches three years?  
**Answer:** Their annualized rate changes from 120 to 160 hours beginning on the third anniversary. If the anniversary falls mid-pay-period, that period's accrual is prorated between the two rates; there is no immediate lump-sum grant of 40 extra hours.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 10. Worked examples > 10.3 Four-day vacation request
chunks.snippet:
**Question:** How many hours should an employee request for four scheduled eight-hour days?  
**Answer:** 32 PTO hours, assuming none of those days is an observed paid holiday.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 10. Worked examples > 10.4 Request made two days ahead
chunks.snippet:
**Question:** Can an employee request vacation with only two business days' notice?  
**Answer:** They can submit the request, but it does not meet the normal five-business-day planned-absence requirement. The manager and People Operations may consider an exception. Urgent or protected absences are handled separately.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 10. Worked examples > 10.5 Request exceeds accrued balance
chunks.snippet:
**Question:** Can someone with 10 accrued hours take 24 hours of PTO next week?  
**Answer:** Not ordinarily. They need enough accrued hours when the absence is processed or a written People Operations exception for advanced PTO, capped at 16 hours under the standard policy. A manager alone cannot authorize a negative balance.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 10. Worked examples > 10.6 Carryover in a restrictive jurisdiction
chunks.snippet:
**Question:** Will 70 unused hours always be reduced to 40 at year-end?  
**Answer:** No. The standard 40-hour carryover cap applies only where lawful. People Operations must apply the employee's jurisdiction-specific requirements before reducing any accrued balance.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 10. Worked examples > 10.7 PTO and parental leave
chunks.snippet:
**Question:** Does parental leave automatically use PTO?  
**Answer:** No universal rule applies. People Operations reviews HR-006, the employee's circumstances, and applicable law to determine pay coordination and any concurrent use.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 11. Frequently asked questions > 11.1 Is PTO front-loaded on January 1?
chunks.snippet: No. PTO accrues over the year in semi-monthly pay periods. Carryover from the prior year may be available at the start of the year.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 11. Frequently asked questions > 11.2 Does a weekend count as PTO?
chunks.snippet: Not if the employee was not scheduled to work. PTO is deducted only for scheduled work hours missed.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 11. Frequently asked questions > 11.3 Who can see my reason for taking PTO?
chunks.snippet: Managers see scheduling information necessary to approve an absence. Employees do not need to include sensitive personal or medical details in ordinary PTO requests.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 11. Frequently asked questions > 11.4 Can a manager deny a vacation request?
chunks.snippet: Yes, for legitimate scheduling or coverage reasons, subject to the fair-review standards in Section 4 and applicable protected-leave laws.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 11. Frequently asked questions > 11.5 Can I carry over more than five days?
chunks.snippet: Under the default policy, no; however, more protective state or local law or a documented written exception may apply.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 11. Frequently asked questions > 11.6 What if I move to a different state?
chunks.snippet: Notify People Operations before the move. Your work location may change the legal rules governing accrual, carryover, paid sick leave, and payout. Remote work location approval is separately governed by HR-004.

chunks.title: Paid Time Off Policy
chunks.section: Paid Time Off Policy > 12. Document control
chunks.snippet: People Operations reviews this policy annually and whenever relevant law or company practice changes. The current approved copy is published in the internal policy repository. Superseded versions must be archived and excluded from the active RAG retrieval index. For questions that depend on state or local law, the chatbot should direct the employee to People Operations rather than infer a jurisdiction-specific entitlement from this general policy.

chunks.title: Holiday Policy
chunks.snippet:
Holiday Policy

Northstar Technologies | Policy HR-003 | Version 1.0

Fictional training document. Northstar Technologies, its contacts, systems, and policies are invented for RAG demonstration. This document does not replace applicable law, plan documents, or written agreements.

1. Purpose and coverage

chunks.title: Holiday Policy
chunks.section: 1.1 Scope
chunks.snippet: Northstar provides designated paid company holidays separately from accrued PTO. HR-002 controls PTO balances; HR-006 controls protected leave. The annual holiday calendar is published in the People Portal before January 1. State or local law and signed agreements control when they provide different rights.

chunks.title: Holiday Policy
chunks.section: 1.2 Eligibility
chunks.snippet:
Regular full-time US employees scheduled for 40 hours are eligible from hire. Employees with approved 30–39-hour schedules receive holiday pay for the hours ordinarily scheduled on the observed day. Other workers may have location-specific statutory entitlements; People Operations confirms eligibility.

2. Observed holiday calendar

chunks.title: Holiday Policy
chunks.section: 2.1 2026 company holidays
chunks.snippet: For 2026, Northstar observes New Year’s Day (January 1), Martin Luther King Jr. Day (January 19), Memorial Day (May 25), Juneteenth (June 19), Independence Day observed (July 3), Labor Day (September 7), Thanksgiving Day (November 26), day after Thanksgiving (November 27), and Christmas Day (December 25). These dates apply to the fictional 2026 calendar; future years require a newly published calendar.

chunks.title: Holiday Policy
chunks.section: 2.2 Weekend observance
chunks.snippet: A fixed-date holiday falling on Saturday is normally observed on the preceding Friday; one falling on Sunday is normally observed on the following Monday. The published calendar is authoritative when an operational exception exists.

chunks.title: Holiday Policy
chunks.section: 2.3 Customer coverage
chunks.snippet:
Support and operations teams may need scheduled holiday coverage. Managers must publish rotations in advance, coordinate with People Operations, and comply with applicable pay and rest requirements. Employees should not assume that working a holiday creates an extra PTO credit.

3. Floating holidays

chunks.title: Holiday Policy
chunks.section: 3.1 Annual allowance
chunks.snippet: Eligible full-time employees receive two floating holidays (16 hours) per calendar year; eligible 30–39-hour employees receive a prorated amount. New hires beginning July 1 or later receive one floating holiday (8 hours for a 40-hour schedule) for that first calendar year.

chunks.title: Holiday Policy
chunks.section: 3.2 Requesting and expiration
chunks.snippet: Request floating-holiday hours in the People Portal at least five business days in advance when practicable. Manager approval follows the normal coverage workflow. Unused floating holidays expire December 31 unless law requires otherwise; they do not carry over under the default plan and are not deducted from accrued PTO.

chunks.title: Holiday Policy
chunks.section: 3.3 Personal observances
chunks.snippet:
Floating holidays may be used for religious, cultural, civic, or personal observances. Employees need not disclose a religious belief to request a floating holiday. Requests for legally required accommodation are handled separately by People Operations.

4. Pay and scheduling rules

chunks.title: Holiday Policy
chunks.section: 4.1 Holiday during PTO
chunks.snippet: An eligible employee on an approved vacation receives holiday pay for normally scheduled hours on an observed company holiday and is not charged PTO for those hours. Example: a Monday–Friday 40-hour employee taking Thanksgiving week uses 24 PTO hours because Thursday and Friday are holidays.

chunks.title: Holiday Policy
chunks.section: 4.2 Holiday during leave
chunks.snippet: Holiday pay during an extended or unpaid leave depends on the leave designation, plan terms, and applicable law. HR-006 and People Operations determine the correct code; employees must not assume a holiday interrupts protected leave.

chunks.title: Holiday Policy
chunks.section: 4.3 Part-time and alternative schedules
chunks.snippet: Holiday hours are based on normally scheduled work on the observed day, subject to local rules. An employee not ordinarily scheduled that day does not automatically receive replacement hours. People Operations can evaluate equitable scheduling alternatives.

chunks.title: Holiday Policy
chunks.section: 4.4 Overtime
chunks.snippet:
For nonexempt employees, paid holiday hours are not treated as hours worked for federal overtime calculations unless applicable law or a written plan requires otherwise. All hours actually worked must be recorded.

5. Procedure and questions

chunks.title: Holiday Policy
chunks.section: 5.1 How to verify
chunks.snippet: Open People Portal → Time Off → Holiday Calendar. Confirm your location and schedule. If the calendar differs from a team announcement, ask People Operations to reconcile before booking travel.

chunks.title: Holiday Policy
chunks.section: 5.2 Frequently asked questions
chunks.snippet: Does a company holiday use my PTO? No, when you qualify for holiday pay. Can I move Christmas Day to another day? Not automatically; request a floating holiday or an accommodation. Can a manager cancel a company holiday? Only through a formally approved coverage plan, not an informal change.

chunks.title: Holiday Policy
chunks.section: 5.3 Escalation
chunks.snippet:
Send eligibility and coding questions to people@northstar.example. Payroll corrections go to payroll@northstar.example. A manager cannot independently change the published company holiday calendar.

6. Document control

People Operations or the responsible policy owner resolves ambiguities; applicable law and governing plan documents prevail where required. Policy updates are published in the People Portal. For policy questions, use the contacts specified above or consult HR-001 Employee Handbook.

chunks.title: Remote Work Policy

Remote Work Policy

Northstar Technologies | Policy HR-004 | Version 1.0

Fictional training document. Northstar Technologies, its contacts, systems, and policies are invented for RAG demonstration. This document does not replace applicable law, plan documents, or written agreements.

1. Scope and work arrangements

chunks.title: Remote Work Policy
chunks.section: 1.1 Arrangement types
chunks.snippet: Northstar uses office-based, hybrid, and fully remote designations. A position’s designation is recorded in the People Portal and may differ by job duties. A remote arrangement does not change performance, confidentiality, timekeeping, or attendance obligations.

chunks.title: Remote Work Policy
chunks.section: 1.2 Hybrid attendance
chunks.snippet: Unless an approved team schedule says otherwise, hybrid employees attend their assigned office Tuesday and Thursday. Managers may coordinate occasional swaps for business reasons; a permanent arrangement change requires People Operations approval.

chunks.title: Remote Work Policy
chunks.section: 1.3 Core collaboration
chunks.snippet:
Most corporate teams coordinate around 9:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. Mountain Time. Employees agree on overlap hours with their manager, keep calendars current, and attend required meetings. Nonexempt employees must accurately record all hours worked.

2. Approval and location

chunks.title: Remote Work Policy
chunks.section: 2.1 Request workflow
chunks.snippet: Submit a work-arrangement request in the People Portal describing location, proposed schedule, business justification, and start date. The manager reviews role suitability and coverage; People Operations reviews employment and tax implications; IT reviews security needs. Do not begin a permanent change until written approval is recorded.

chunks.title: Remote Work Policy
chunks.section: 2.2 Working from another state
chunks.snippet: Even a temporary two-week stay in another US state requires written approval from People Operations before travel. Submit the request at least 15 business days in advance where practical. Approval is not guaranteed; tax registration, payroll, insurance, and customer restrictions may prevent it.

chunks.title: Remote Work Policy
chunks.section: 2.3 International work
chunks.snippet: Working outside the United States is prohibited unless People Operations, Legal, and Security provide explicit written approval before departure. A vacation trip does not authorize working abroad.

chunks.title: Remote Work Policy
chunks.section: 2.4 Address changes
chunks.snippet:
Update your actual work location in the People Portal within five business days of an approved move. A mailing-address update alone does not authorize a new work location.

3. Workspace and technology

chunks.title: Remote Work Policy
chunks.section: 3.1 Privacy and ergonomics
chunks.snippet: Use a reasonably private, safe workspace. Lock your screen when away, prevent household members from seeing company data, and avoid discussing confidential matters in public. Report ergonomic concerns to People Operations.

chunks.title: Remote Work Policy
chunks.section: 3.2 Approved devices
chunks.snippet: Use managed company devices for company work unless IT grants a written exception. Personal or shared computers and personal cloud drives are not approved for storing company data. IT-001 controls equipment provisioning and returns.

chunks.title: Remote Work Policy
chunks.section: 3.3 Connectivity and outages
chunks.snippet:
Employees are responsible for reliable internet access. If connectivity fails, promptly notify the manager, open an IT ticket if applicable, and agree on alternate work or leave coding. Never record hours not worked.

4. Security and expenses

chunks.title: Remote Work Policy
chunks.section: 4.1 Data security
chunks.snippet: Use company VPN or other approved access controls when required, MFA, and approved collaboration systems. Do not print sensitive customer records at home without Security approval. SEC-001 governs incident reporting and data classification.

chunks.title: Remote Work Policy
chunks.section: 4.2 Home-office costs
chunks.snippet: Northstar does not automatically reimburse personal internet, utilities, furniture, or rent. Required business expenses and approved equipment are handled under FIN-001 and IT-001, subject to applicable reimbursement law.

chunks.title: Remote Work Policy
chunks.section: 4.3 Travel to office
chunks.snippet:
Ordinary commuting to the assigned office is generally not reimbursable. Required travel to another business location may qualify under FIN-001 with preapproval.

5. Exceptions and enforcement

chunks.title: Remote Work Policy
chunks.section: 5.1 Accommodation requests
chunks.snippet: Employees seeking disability-related or other legally protected adjustments should contact People Operations. An accommodation request is reviewed separately from discretionary remote-work eligibility.

chunks.title: Remote Work Policy
chunks.section: 5.2 Performance and review
chunks.snippet: Managers review arrangements when roles or business needs change. Any material change is communicated in writing with reasonable notice, subject to law and agreements. Violations may result in revised access or disciplinary action.

chunks.title: Remote Work Policy
chunks.section: 5.3 Examples
chunks.snippet:
Can I work from a hotel in another state for two weeks? Not without prior written People Operations approval. Can I use a family laptop if mine breaks? No, contact IT-002 for a loaner. Can my manager approve a permanent relocation alone? No.

6. Document control

People Operations or the responsible policy owner resolves ambiguities; applicable law and governing plan documents prevail where required. Policy updates are published in the People Portal. chunks.snippet:
Expense Reimbursement Policy

Northstar Technologies | Policy FIN-001 | Version 1.0

Fictional training document. Northstar Technologies, its contacts, systems, and policies are invented for RAG demonstration. This document does not replace applicable law, plan documents, or written agreements.

1. Principles and authority

chunks.title: Expense Reimbursement Policy
chunks.section: 1.1 Business purpose
chunks.snippet: Northstar reimburses reasonable, necessary, documented expenses incurred for authorized company business, subject to applicable law. Employees must use the fictional Northstar Expense Portal and provide an accurate business purpose.

chunks.title: Expense Reimbursement Policy
chunks.section: 1.2 Approvals
chunks.snippet: A manager confirms business necessity and budget; Finance checks policy and documentation. Employees may not approve their own expenses. A manager’s verbal approval does not replace required written preapproval.

chunks.title: Expense Reimbursement Policy
chunks.section: 1.3 Deadlines
chunks.snippet:
Submit reimbursement claims within 30 calendar days of the transaction when practical. Finance targets payment within 15 business days after a complete claim is approved. Late claims are reviewed under applicable reimbursement law rather than automatically forfeited.

2. Travel and lodging

chunks.title: Expense Reimbursement Policy
chunks.section: 2.1 Travel preapproval
chunks.snippet: Obtain manager approval in the Expense Portal before booking flights, hotels, or rental cars. Air travel is economy class unless Finance grants an exception. Book reasonable fares and retain itinerary and proof of payment.

chunks.title: Expense Reimbursement Policy
chunks.section: 2.2 Lodging
chunks.snippet: Use standard business lodging near the work site. Nightly room rates above $225 before taxes require written Finance approval before booking, except when a designated conference hotel or market conditions justify an exception.

chunks.title: Expense Reimbursement Policy
chunks.section: 2.3 Meals
chunks.snippet: For approved overnight business travel, actual reasonable meal costs are reimbursable up to $75 per traveler per day including tips and taxes, with itemized receipts. Alcohol is not reimbursable under the standard plan. Client entertainment requires documented attendee names and business purpose.

chunks.title: Expense Reimbursement Policy
chunks.section: 2.4 Ground transportation
chunks.snippet:
Use cost-effective public transit, ride-share, or rental cars. Personal vehicle business mileage is reimbursed at the applicable company-published rate, not for normal commuting. Record origin, destination, business purpose, and miles.

3. Purchases and equipment

chunks.title: Expense Reimbursement Policy
chunks.section: 3.1 Preapproval thresholds
chunks.snippet: Any single non-travel purchase above $250 requires written manager preapproval; purchases above $1,000 also require Finance approval. Splitting a purchase to avoid a threshold is prohibited.

chunks.title: Expense Reimbursement Policy
chunks.section: 3.2 Home office
chunks.snippet: Home-office furniture and personal internet are not automatically covered. IT-001 governs managed laptops and standard accessories. State-required reimbursement may apply even where company policy would otherwise exclude an item.

chunks.title: Expense Reimbursement Policy
chunks.section: 3.3 Training
chunks.snippet:
Role-related courses, conferences, and certifications require manager preapproval, including cost and expected benefit. Optional personal subscriptions are not automatically reimbursable.

4. Receipts and processing

chunks.title: Expense Reimbursement Policy
chunks.section: 4.1 Required evidence
chunks.snippet: For expenses of $25 or more, attach an itemized receipt and proof of payment; for smaller expenses provide available evidence and a business explanation. Credit-card summaries alone may be insufficient to establish items purchased. Finance may request additional evidence.

chunks.title: Expense Reimbursement Policy
chunks.section: 4.2 Submission steps
chunks.snippet: 1. Open Expense Portal → New Claim. 2. Select category and cost center. 3. Enter date, merchant, currency, amount, and business purpose. 4. Attach receipts and preapprovals. 5. Submit to manager; Finance reviews after manager approval.

chunks.title: Expense Reimbursement Policy
chunks.section: 4.3 Currencies and refunds
chunks.snippet: Enter the original currency and amount; the portal converts at the approved processing rate. Report refunds, credits, or canceled travel promptly and return duplicate reimbursements.

chunks.title: Expense Reimbursement Policy
chunks.section: 4.4 Corporate cards
chunks.snippet:
Corporate cards are for authorized company expenses only. Report loss or suspected fraud immediately to Finance and Security when appropriate. Never submit a card-paid expense as a personal reimbursement.

5. Exceptions and scenarios

chunks.title: Expense Reimbursement Policy
chunks.section: 5.1 Nonreimbursable examples
chunks.snippet: Personal entertainment, fines, normal commuting, companion travel, personal upgrades, unapproved gifts, and unsupported duplicate claims are normally excluded. Legally required reimbursements are not waived by this list.

chunks.title: Expense Reimbursement Policy
chunks.section: 5.2 Scenario: $280 monitor
chunks.snippet: A remote employee should request IT approval under IT-001 before buying a monitor. Because the purchase exceeds $250, manager preapproval is also required if personal purchase is authorized; Finance confirms reimbursement eligibility.

chunks.title: Expense Reimbursement Policy
chunks.section: 5.3 Scenario: $90 dinner
chunks.snippet: An employee on approved overnight travel spends $90 on an individual dinner. The daily $75 meal cap applies to total meals that day, so reimbursement is limited absent a documented exception.

chunks.title: Expense Reimbursement Policy
chunks.section: 5.4 Disputes and contacts
chunks.snippet:
Ask expenses@northstar.example for status or corrections. Escalate unresolved policy disputes to the Finance Operations lead; concerns about retaliation can be reported through HR-007.

chunks.title: Data Security Policy

chunks.snippet: Protect Northstar customer data, employee information, intellectual property, and service availability. Everyone with access to company systems must follow this policy, regardless of work location.

chunks.snippet: **Public** data is approved for release. **Internal** data is routine nonpublic business information. **Confidential** data includes contracts, customer records, personnel information, and nonpublic financial data. **Restricted** data includes credentials, authentication secrets, sensitive personal data, and production secrets. chunks.title: Data Security Policy

chunks.title: Data Security Policy
chunks.section: Data Security Policy > 2. Authentication and devices > 2.1 MFA
chunks.snippet: Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for company identity, email, VPN, and other supported systems. Never approve an unexpected MFA prompt. Report repeated prompts immediately.

chunks.title: Data Security Policy
chunks.section: Data Security Policy > 2. Authentication and devices > 2.2 Passwords
chunks.snippet: Use company-approved password managers and unique credentials. Do not reuse company passwords on personal sites, send passwords in chat, or store secrets in source repositories. IT-002 handles account recovery after identity verification.

chunks.title: Data Security Policy
chunks.section: Data Security Policy > 2. Authentication and devices > 2.3 Managed endpoints
chunks.snippet: Company laptops must use enforced screen locks, full-disk encryption, automatic updates, and endpoint protection. Do not disable controls or install unapproved software. Report lost devices immediately even if encrypted.

chunks.title: Data Security Policy
chunks.section: Data Security Policy > 2. Authentication and devices > 2.4 Remote access
chunks.snippet: Use approved secure access methods and avoid unknown public computers. Personal cloud storage, unauthorized USB transfers, and forwarding company email to personal accounts are prohibited.

chunks.title: Data Security Policy
chunks.section: Data Security Policy > 3. Sharing, retention, and AI > 3.1 Minimum necessary sharing
chunks.snippet: Share only the minimum necessary data with authorized recipients in approved company tools. Verify recipient identities and external domains before sending Confidential information. Restricted information requires explicit approved access.

chunks.title: Data Security Policy
chunks.section: Data Security Policy > 3. Sharing, retention, and AI > 3.2 Data retention
chunks.snippet: Retain records according to the approved retention schedule and any legal hold. Do not delete records to conceal an error or suspected incident. Ask Security or Legal before exporting large datasets.

chunks.title: Data Security Policy
chunks.section: Data Security Policy > 3. Sharing, retention, and AI > 3.3 Generative AI
chunks.snippet: Do not paste Confidential or Restricted company information, customer records, source code, or credentials into public AI services. Use only company-approved AI tools for approved data classes and follow vendor-specific controls. Human review remains required for consequential outputs.

chunks.title: Data Security Policy
chunks.section: Data Security Policy > 3. Sharing, retention, and AI > 3.4 External sharing
chunks.snippet: External vendors require approved contracts, security review, and appropriate access controls before receiving Confidential data. A customer request does not override classification requirements.

chunks.title: Data Security Policy
chunks.section: Data Security Policy > 4. Incident reporting and response > 4.1 What counts as an incident
chunks.snippet: Examples include phishing clicks, unexpected MFA requests, lost laptops, malware warnings, mistaken email recipients, exposed credentials, and suspicious access. A suspected incident is reportable even without confirmed harm.

chunks.title: Data Security Policy
chunks.section: Data Security Policy > 4. Incident reporting and response > 4.2 Immediate steps
chunks.snippet: 1. Stop the risky action. 2. Report immediately through IT Service Desk or security@northstar.example. 3. Provide time, device, affected systems, and what occurred. 4. Follow Security instructions. Do not investigate independently, erase evidence, or conceal mistakes.

chunks.title: Data Security Policy
chunks.section: Data Security Policy > 4. Incident reporting and response > 4.3 Lost device
chunks.snippet: Contact Security and IT immediately, stating the device identifier, last known location, and whether any customer data was stored locally. IT may remotely lock or wipe the device; only IT authorizes that action.

chunks.title: Data Security Policy
chunks.section: Data Security Policy > 4. Incident reporting and response > 4.4 Mistaken disclosure
chunks.snippet: If a Confidential file was sent to the wrong recipient, report immediately; do not assume recalling an email solved the problem. Security coordinates containment, notification, and documentation.

chunks.title: Data Security Policy
chunks.section: Data Security Policy > 4. Incident reporting and response > 4.5 Communication
chunks.snippet: Only authorized incident responders communicate externally about security incidents. Do not speculate about breach impact in public channels or customer conversations.

chunks.title: Data Security Policy
chunks.section: Data Security Policy > 5. Training, compliance, and examples > 5.1 Training
chunks.snippet: Employees complete security orientation during onboarding and annual refresher training. Role-specific access may require additional training.

chunks.title: Data Security Policy
chunks.section: Data Security Policy > 5. Training, compliance, and examples > 5.2 Example: suspicious link
chunks.snippet: An employee clicks a phishing link but does not enter a password. They must still report it immediately; Security determines whether further action is needed.

chunks.title: Data Security Policy
chunks.section: Data Security Policy > 5. Training, compliance, and examples > 5.3 Example: AI summarization
chunks.snippet: An employee may not paste a customer contract into an unapproved public chatbot for summarization. They should request an approved workflow from Security.

chunks.title: Data Security Policy
chunks.section: Data Security Policy > 5. Training, compliance, and examples > 5.4 Questions and escalation
chunks.snippet: Routine access issues go to helpdesk@northstar.example. Suspected incidents go immediately to security@northstar.example. Retaliation for good-faith reporting is prohibited under HR-007.

chunks.title: Employee Benefits Guide
chunks.section: Employee Benefits Guide > 1. Overview and eligibility > 1.1 Purpose and authority
chunks.snippet: This fictional guide summarizes Northstar benefits for training. Governing insurance contracts, plan documents, applicable law, and individualized enrollment notices control over this summary.

chunks.title: Employee Benefits Guide
chunks.section: Employee Benefits Guide > 1. Overview and eligibility > 1.2 Eligible employees
chunks.snippet: Regular full-time US employees scheduled for 40 hours are generally eligible. Employees scheduled for 30–39 hours are evaluated by People Operations under plan and legal requirements. Contractors and agency workers are not automatically eligible.

chunks.title: Employee Benefits Guide
chunks.section: Employee Benefits Guide > 1. Overview and eligibility > 1.3 Coverage start
chunks.snippet: For eligible new hires, medical, dental, and vision coverage normally starts on the first day of the month following the hire date, subject to timely enrollment and plan rules. If hired on the first day of a month, coverage normally starts that day.

chunks.title: Employee Benefits Guide
chunks.section: Employee Benefits Guide > 2. Health and welfare plans > 2.1 Medical
chunks.snippet: Northstar offers a fictional PPO option and high-deductible health plan option. Premiums, deductibles, networks, and covered services vary by plan and year; review the current plan comparison in the People Portal rather than relying on a quoted example.

chunks.title: Employee Benefits Guide
chunks.section: Employee Benefits Guide > 2. Health and welfare plans > 2.2 Dental and vision
chunks.snippet: Eligible employees may elect dental and vision plans for themselves and eligible dependents. Coverage levels and annual limits are governed by the respective plan documents.

chunks.title: Employee Benefits Guide
chunks.section: Employee Benefits Guide > 2. Health and welfare plans > 2.3 Life and disability
chunks.snippet: Northstar provides a basic employer-paid life insurance benefit for eligible employees and offers optional supplemental coverage. Short- and long-term disability benefits may be available subject to eligibility, waiting periods, and policy terms.

chunks.title: Employee Benefits Guide
chunks.section: Employee Benefits Guide > 2. Health and welfare plans > 2.4 Employee assistance
chunks.snippet: A confidential employee assistance program offers short-term counseling and referral resources. The program is not a substitute for emergency services.

chunks.title: Employee Benefits Guide
chunks.section: Employee Benefits Guide > 3. Retirement and other support > 3.1 401(k) plan
chunks.snippet: Eligible employees may participate in the fictional Northstar 401(k) plan subject to plan eligibility and enrollment rules. Northstar’s illustrative matching formula is 100% of employee contributions up to 4% of eligible pay; vesting and contribution limits follow the governing plan.

chunks.title: Employee Benefits Guide
chunks.section: Employee Benefits Guide > 3. Retirement and other support > 3.2 Health savings account
chunks.snippet: Employees enrolled in an HSA-eligible high-deductible plan may be able to contribute to an HSA, subject to tax rules and eligibility. People Operations cannot provide individualized tax advice.

chunks.title: Employee Benefits Guide
chunks.section: Employee Benefits Guide > 3. Retirement and other support > 3.3 Wellness and learning
chunks.snippet: Optional wellness resources and approved professional development may be offered. Expenses for courses or conferences follow FIN-001 and do not automatically qualify as benefit claims.

chunks.title: Employee Benefits Guide
chunks.section: Employee Benefits Guide > 4. Enrollment and changes > 4.1 New-hire window
chunks.snippet: Eligible new hires should submit elections through People Portal → Benefits within 30 calendar days of their hire date, unless a different legally required or plan-specific deadline applies. Missing the window may delay changes until open enrollment or a qualifying event.

chunks.title: Employee Benefits Guide
chunks.section: Employee Benefits Guide > 4. Enrollment and changes > 4.2 Annual open enrollment
chunks.snippet: People Operations announces dates, premiums, and plan changes before each annual open enrollment period. Elections generally apply to the following plan year, subject to plan terms.

chunks.title: Employee Benefits Guide
chunks.section: Employee Benefits Guide > 4. Enrollment and changes > 4.3 Qualifying life events
chunks.snippet: Marriage, birth or adoption, loss of other coverage, and certain employment changes may permit midyear elections. Notify People Operations promptly, normally within 30 calendar days of the event, and provide required documentation. Some events have different legal deadlines.

chunks.title: Employee Benefits Guide
chunks.section: Employee Benefits Guide > 4. Enrollment and changes > 4.4 Dependents
chunks.snippet: Employees must certify dependent eligibility and update coverage when a dependent no longer qualifies. Knowingly inaccurate enrollment information may result in correction or other action consistent with law.

chunks.title: Employee Benefits Guide
chunks.section: Employee Benefits Guide > 5. Leave, privacy, and assistance > 5.1 Benefits during leave
chunks.snippet: Continuation of coverage and premium payment obligations during paid or unpaid leave depend on HR-006, plan terms, and applicable law. People Operations provides individualized instructions.

chunks.title: Employee Benefits Guide
chunks.section: Employee Benefits Guide > 5. Leave, privacy, and assistance > 5.2 Separation
chunks.snippet: On separation, People Operations provides notices about coverage termination and continuation rights where applicable. Do not assume all benefits end on the last workday.

chunks.title: Employee Benefits Guide
chunks.section: Employee Benefits Guide > 5. Leave, privacy, and assistance > 5.3 Privacy
chunks.snippet: Medical claims and diagnoses should be shared with the insurer or designated benefits administrator, not a line manager. People Operations limits access to sensitive information.

chunks.title: Employee Benefits Guide
chunks.section: Employee Benefits Guide > 5. Leave, privacy, and assistance > 5.4 Examples and contacts
chunks.snippet: **I was hired June 10; when does coverage normally begin?** July 1 if eligible and timely enrolled. **Can I change plans after having a baby?** Potentially, through the qualifying-event process. Contact people@northstar.example for plan-specific details.
