chunks.title: Onboarding Procedures
chunks.section: Onboarding Procedures > 1. Ownership and preparation > 1.1 Purpose
chunks.snippet: This procedure defines a consistent new-hire experience. People Operations coordinates employment records; managers coordinate role readiness; IT provisions approved technology and access.

chunks.title: Onboarding Procedures
chunks.section: Onboarding Procedures > 1. Ownership and preparation > 1.2 Before start date
chunks.snippet: People Operations sends a welcome packet, required employment forms, and People Portal instructions through approved channels. Managers assign an onboarding buddy and prepare a first-week agenda. IT records a device request and approved access list.

chunks.title: Onboarding Procedures
chunks.section: Onboarding Procedures > 1. Ownership and preparation > 1.3 Sensitive documents
chunks.snippet: Submit identity, tax, and banking information only through the approved People Portal or authorized secure process. Do not email scans of identity documents to a manager or personal inbox.

chunks.title: Onboarding Procedures
chunks.section: Onboarding Procedures > 2. Day-one checklist > 2.1 People Operations
chunks.snippet: Verify onboarding tasks, work location, employment classification, payroll details, and required notices. Complete employment eligibility verification within applicable legal deadlines; ask People Operations about any accessibility or accommodation needs.

chunks.title: Onboarding Procedures
chunks.section: Onboarding Procedures > 2. Day-one checklist > 2.2 IT setup
chunks.snippet: Receive managed laptop and approved accessories, verify device inventory tag, enroll MFA, confirm password manager, and test email, collaboration tools, and VPN or approved secure access.

chunks.title: Onboarding Procedures
chunks.section: Onboarding Procedures > 2. Day-one checklist > 2.3 Manager introduction
chunks.snippet: Review role outcomes, team contacts, core hours, communication norms, hybrid schedule, and first 30-day goals. Introduce the onboarding buddy and explain how to ask for help.

chunks.title: Onboarding Procedures
chunks.section: Onboarding Procedures > 2. Day-one checklist > 2.4 Security orientation
chunks.snippet: Complete initial security training before receiving sensitive production access. Confirm how to report suspicious messages, lost devices, and accidental disclosures.

chunks.title: Onboarding Procedures
chunks.section: Onboarding Procedures > 3. First week and first month > 3.1 First week
chunks.snippet: Complete required policy acknowledgments, benefits enrollment orientation, payroll verification, and tool training. Managers review the first meaningful work assignment and expected deliverables.

chunks.title: Onboarding Procedures
chunks.section: Onboarding Procedures > 3. First week and first month > 3.2 Benefits enrollment
chunks.snippet: Eligible new hires generally have 30 calendar days from hire to submit benefit elections under BEN-001, subject to plan-specific rules. A manager cannot extend an enrollment deadline.

chunks.title: Onboarding Procedures
chunks.section: Onboarding Procedures > 3. First week and first month > 3.3 Thirty-day check-in
chunks.snippet: Manager and employee review onboarding blockers, access needs, training progress, and expectations. People Operations resolves any employment or benefits issues that require confidential handling.

chunks.title: Onboarding Procedures
chunks.section: Onboarding Procedures > 3. First week and first month > 3.4 Sixty- and ninety-day check-ins
chunks.snippet: Managers provide structured feedback and update development goals. These check-ins do not create a universal probationary period or override employment rights.

chunks.title: Onboarding Procedures
chunks.section: Onboarding Procedures > 4. Access and exceptions > 4.1 Least privilege
chunks.snippet: Managers request only access needed for the employee’s role. IT and application owners approve access according to SEC-001. Access to Restricted data requires additional justification and training.

chunks.title: Onboarding Procedures
chunks.section: Onboarding Procedures > 4. Access and exceptions > 4.2 Equipment delay
chunks.snippet: If a laptop is delayed, IT may issue a managed loaner. New hires must not use a personal or shared household computer for company data without written IT authorization.

chunks.title: Onboarding Procedures
chunks.section: Onboarding Procedures > 4. Access and exceptions > 4.3 Remote hires
chunks.snippet: People Operations verifies approved work location under HR-004; IT arranges secure shipment. Remote employees must follow the same security and timekeeping rules as office-based employees.

chunks.title: Onboarding Procedures
chunks.section: Onboarding Procedures > 5. Completion and escalation > 5.1 Completion record
chunks.snippet: The manager confirms role readiness; People Operations records policy acknowledgments and required onboarding forms; IT closes provisioning tickets only after access checks.

chunks.title: Onboarding Procedures
chunks.section: Onboarding Procedures > 5. Completion and escalation > 5.2 Example: missing MFA
chunks.snippet: A new hire cannot access email because MFA enrollment failed. They contact helpdesk@northstar.example, complete identity verification, and use the IT-002 recovery process; they do not borrow a colleague’s login.

chunks.title: Onboarding Procedures
chunks.section: Onboarding Procedures > 5. Completion and escalation > 5.3 Where to ask
chunks.snippet: Employment and benefits: people@northstar.example. Device or login: helpdesk@northstar.example. Security concerns: security@northstar.example. Payroll: payroll@northstar.example.

chunks.title: Equipment Policy
chunks.section: Equipment Policy > 1. Equipment ownership > 1.1 Standard issue
chunks.snippet: Northstar ordinarily provides one managed laptop, charger, and required security accessories to employees whose roles need them. Role-specific peripherals are approved by IT based on documented business need.

chunks.title: Equipment Policy
chunks.section: Equipment Policy > 1. Equipment ownership > 1.2 Ownership and inventory
chunks.snippet: Company-issued equipment remains Northstar property. IT records asset tag, serial number, assigned employee, issue date, and return status. Employees may not sell, lend, or transfer equipment without IT authorization.

chunks.title: Equipment Policy
chunks.section: Equipment Policy > 1. Equipment ownership > 1.3 Personal devices
chunks.snippet: Personal or shared devices are not approved for storing or processing company data unless IT issues a documented exception with required controls.

chunks.title: Equipment Policy
chunks.section: Equipment Policy > 2. Requests and approvals > 2.1 New-hire provisioning
chunks.snippet: Managers submit device and access needs through the IT Service Desk before the employee’s start date. IT selects standard hardware; exceptions require IT Operations approval.

chunks.title: Equipment Policy
chunks.section: Equipment Policy > 2. Requests and approvals > 2.2 Accessory requests
chunks.snippet: Request monitors, headsets, keyboards, and ergonomic accessories through IT Service Desk with business justification. Do not purchase first and assume reimbursement.

chunks.title: Equipment Policy
chunks.section: Equipment Policy > 2. Requests and approvals > 2.3 Purchase coordination
chunks.snippet: If IT authorizes an employee purchase, FIN-001 reimbursement thresholds and receipts still apply. A $280 monitor requires IT authorization and manager preapproval before purchase; Finance confirms eligibility.

chunks.title: Equipment Policy
chunks.section: Equipment Policy > 2. Requests and approvals > 2.4 Replacement cycle
chunks.snippet: IT evaluates standard laptops for replacement around the fourth year of service or sooner when security, warranty, or performance needs justify it. Replacement is not an automatic employee entitlement.

chunks.title: Equipment Policy
chunks.section: Equipment Policy > 3. Care and security > 3.1 Daily use
chunks.snippet: Keep devices physically secure, lock screens, install required updates, and use approved storage and collaboration tools. Do not disable encryption or endpoint controls.

chunks.title: Equipment Policy
chunks.section: Equipment Policy > 3. Care and security > 3.2 Travel and remote work
chunks.snippet: Carry laptops in hand luggage where practical and avoid leaving them unattended in public or vehicles. Remote employees follow HR-004 workspace rules.

chunks.title: Equipment Policy
chunks.section: Equipment Policy > 3. Care and security > 3.3 Damage and loss
chunks.snippet: Report lost, stolen, or damaged equipment immediately to IT Service Desk. Suspected theft or data exposure must also be reported immediately to Security under SEC-001. Do not attempt unauthorized repairs.

chunks.title: Equipment Policy
chunks.section: Equipment Policy > 3. Care and security > 3.4 Personal use
chunks.snippet: Incidental personal use may be allowed if lawful and consistent with security rules, but company devices are primarily for work and remain subject to authorized administration and monitoring.

chunks.title: Equipment Policy
chunks.section: Equipment Policy > 4. Support and return > 4.1 Repair workflow
chunks.snippet: Open a ticket with asset tag, symptoms, location, and business impact. IT determines remote troubleshooting, repair, loaner, or replacement. Never ship a device to an unapproved vendor.

chunks.title: Equipment Policy
chunks.section: Equipment Policy > 4. Support and return > 4.2 Offboarding
chunks.snippet: On separation or role change, follow IT return instructions and deadlines. Normally ship or return equipment within five business days after the final workday using the provided label or office drop-off process; applicable law controls any deductions.

chunks.title: Equipment Policy
chunks.section: Equipment Policy > 4. Support and return > 4.3 Data handling
chunks.snippet: Do not wipe, sell, or copy company files before returning a device. IT performs approved retention and secure erasure; personal files on company devices may not be recoverable.

chunks.title: Equipment Policy
chunks.section: Equipment Policy > 4. Support and return > 4.4 Examples
chunks.snippet: **My laptop broke during travel.** Report it to IT and request a managed loaner. **Can I give my old laptop to a teammate?** No, IT must reassign it. **Can I expense a desk chair?** Ask IT and Finance first; reimbursement is not automatic.

chunks.title: Leave of Absence Policy
chunks.section: Leave of Absence Policy > 1. Scope and principles > 1.1 Purpose
chunks.snippet: This policy covers extended or protected absences, including medical, family, parental, bereavement, jury duty, military service, and discretionary personal leave. Eligibility and protections depend on law, work location, and individual circumstances.

chunks.title: Leave of Absence Policy
chunks.section: Leave of Absence Policy > 1. Scope and principles > 1.2 Relationship to PTO
chunks.snippet: HR-002 covers ordinary accrued PTO. An absence may qualify for protected leave even when an employee has no PTO balance. People Operations determines when paid leave may run concurrently with protected leave, consistent with applicable law.

chunks.title: Leave of Absence Policy
chunks.section: Leave of Absence Policy > 1. Scope and principles > 1.3 Privacy and nonretaliation
chunks.snippet: Employees should provide sensitive medical documentation to People Operations or an authorized administrator, not a line manager. Retaliation for requesting legally protected leave is prohibited.

chunks.title: Leave of Absence Policy
chunks.section: Leave of Absence Policy > 2. Requesting leave > 2.1 Planned leave
chunks.snippet: Notify People Operations and the manager as early as practicable, ordinarily at least 30 calendar days ahead when the need is foreseeable and the law permits. The manager receives scheduling information, not confidential diagnoses.

chunks.title: Leave of Absence Policy
chunks.section: Leave of Absence Policy > 2. Requesting leave > 2.2 Unexpected leave
chunks.snippet: For emergencies, notify the manager as soon as reasonably possible and contact People Operations when able. The ordinary five-business-day PTO notice rule does not delay urgent or protected leave.

chunks.title: Leave of Absence Policy
chunks.section: Leave of Absence Policy > 2. Requesting leave > 2.3 Documentation
chunks.snippet: People Operations explains eligibility, required forms, certification deadlines, benefits, and return-to-work steps in writing. Employees should respond within stated lawful deadlines; extensions or accommodations may be available.

chunks.title: Leave of Absence Policy
chunks.section: Leave of Absence Policy > 2. Requesting leave > 2.4 Approval authority
chunks.snippet: People Operations determines statutory and company leave eligibility. Managers coordinate coverage but cannot deny a protected leave because of staffing preferences.

chunks.title: Leave of Absence Policy
chunks.section: Leave of Absence Policy > 3. Leave categories > 3.1 Medical and family leave
chunks.snippet: Eligible employees may qualify for job-protected leave under federal, state, or local laws. The applicable entitlement, measurement period, pay status, and documentation are determined case by case.

chunks.title: Leave of Absence Policy
chunks.section: Leave of Absence Policy > 3. Leave categories > 3.2 Parental leave
chunks.snippet: Northstar offers up to six weeks of company-paid bonding leave for eligible regular full-time employees after birth, adoption, or qualifying placement, subject to written plan terms and coordination with legally required benefits. People Operations confirms eligibility and concurrent leave rules before leave begins.

chunks.title: Leave of Absence Policy
chunks.section: Leave of Absence Policy > 3. Leave categories > 3.3 Bereavement
chunks.snippet: Regular full-time employees may request up to three paid workdays following the death of an immediate family member, with up to five days when significant travel is required and People Operations approves. Additional time may be covered by PTO, unpaid leave, or local law.

chunks.title: Leave of Absence Policy
chunks.section: Leave of Absence Policy > 3. Leave categories > 3.4 Jury duty and military service
chunks.snippet: Notify People Operations promptly after receiving a summons or orders. Pay, reinstatement, and benefit protections follow applicable law; do not assume PTO must be used.

chunks.title: Leave of Absence Policy
chunks.section: Leave of Absence Policy > 3. Leave categories > 3.5 Personal leave
chunks.snippet: Employees may request discretionary unpaid personal leave for circumstances not covered by protected leave. Approval is not guaranteed and requires manager and People Operations review.

chunks.title: Leave of Absence Policy
chunks.section: Leave of Absence Policy > 4. Pay, benefits, and accrual > 4.1 Pay during leave
chunks.snippet: Some leave is unpaid; other leave may be paid by Northstar, accrued PTO, insurance, or statutory programs. People Operations provides an individualized written designation and pay summary.

chunks.title: Leave of Absence Policy
chunks.section: Leave of Absence Policy > 4. Pay, benefits, and accrual > 4.2 PTO accrual
chunks.snippet: Under the standard HR-002 plan, PTO accrues during paid working time and paid PTO but is generally suspended for unpaid leave days unless law or a written arrangement requires otherwise.

chunks.title: Leave of Absence Policy
chunks.section: Leave of Absence Policy > 4. Pay, benefits, and accrual > 4.3 Holiday pay
chunks.snippet: Holiday pay during leave is determined under HR-003, the specific leave designation, and applicable law. Employees should not independently code company holidays.

chunks.title: Leave of Absence Policy
chunks.section: Leave of Absence Policy > 4. Pay, benefits, and accrual > 4.4 Benefit continuation
chunks.snippet: Medical coverage, premium payments, and other benefits during leave depend on BEN-001, governing plan terms, and law. People Operations explains employee payment obligations.

chunks.title: Leave of Absence Policy
chunks.section: Leave of Absence Policy > 5. Return and examples > 5.1 Return-to-work coordination
chunks.snippet: Before the expected return, contact People Operations about required clearance, accommodations, scheduling, and system access. Medical clearance is requested only where lawful and appropriate.

chunks.title: Leave of Absence Policy
chunks.section: Leave of Absence Policy > 5. Return and examples > 5.2 Example: new parent
chunks.snippet: An employee expecting a child contacts People Operations in advance. People Operations evaluates statutory leave, the six-week company-paid bonding benefit, benefits continuation, and any requested PTO without assuming all periods add together.

chunks.title: Leave of Absence Policy
chunks.section: Leave of Absence Policy > 5. Return and examples > 5.3 Example: sudden illness
chunks.snippet: An employee unexpectedly needs extended medical leave. They notify the manager when practicable, contact People Operations, and receive individualized instructions; the manager should not demand a diagnosis.

chunks.title: Leave of Absence Policy
chunks.section: Leave of Absence Policy > 5. Return and examples > 5.4 Contact
chunks.snippet: Send leave and accommodation questions to people@northstar.example. Report suspected retaliation or discrimination through ethics@northstar.example.

chunks.title: Workplace Conduct Policy
chunks.section: Workplace Conduct Policy > 1. Standards and scope > 1.1 Respectful conduct
chunks.snippet: Employees must treat colleagues, customers, contractors, and visitors professionally in offices, remote meetings, work chat, travel, and company-sponsored events.

chunks.title: Workplace Conduct Policy
chunks.section: Workplace Conduct Policy > 1. Standards and scope > 1.2 Harassment and discrimination
chunks.snippet: Northstar prohibits unlawful harassment, discrimination, bullying, threats, and abusive conduct. Protected characteristics and legal protections vary by jurisdiction; People Operations applies the governing law.

chunks.title: Workplace Conduct Policy
chunks.section: Workplace Conduct Policy > 1. Standards and scope > 1.3 Examples
chunks.snippet: Examples include repeated derogatory comments, unwelcome sexual remarks, intimidation, exclusionary behavior tied to protected status, and abusive messages in collaboration tools. An isolated incident may still require review.

chunks.title: Workplace Conduct Policy
chunks.section: Workplace Conduct Policy > 2. Conflicts, gifts, and integrity > 2.1 Conflicts of interest
chunks.snippet: Disclose personal, financial, or family interests that could affect purchasing, hiring, vendor selection, or access to confidential information. A disclosed conflict is reviewed; disclosure does not automatically imply wrongdoing.

chunks.title: Workplace Conduct Policy
chunks.section: Workplace Conduct Policy > 2. Conflicts, gifts, and integrity > 2.2 Gifts and hospitality
chunks.snippet: Do not accept cash gifts from vendors. Noncash gifts exceeding $100 in estimated value require disclosure to People Operations and Finance; stricter customer or anti-bribery rules take precedence.

chunks.title: Workplace Conduct Policy
chunks.section: Workplace Conduct Policy > 2. Conflicts, gifts, and integrity > 2.3 Honest records
chunks.snippet: Accurately report work hours, expenses, certifications, and business results. Fabricating timecards or receipts is prohibited. Suspected fraud should be reported through approved channels.

chunks.title: Workplace Conduct Policy
chunks.section: Workplace Conduct Policy > 2. Conflicts, gifts, and integrity > 2.4 Confidentiality
chunks.snippet: Respect personnel and customer privacy and follow SEC-001. Do not share internal investigation details with people who lack a legitimate need to know.

chunks.title: Workplace Conduct Policy
chunks.section: Workplace Conduct Policy > 3. Reporting concerns > 3.1 Reporting options
chunks.snippet: Employees may report concerns to their manager, People Operations at people@northstar.example, or the confidential ethics channel ethics@northstar.example. Employees may bypass a manager who is involved in the concern.

chunks.title: Workplace Conduct Policy
chunks.section: Workplace Conduct Policy > 3. Reporting concerns > 3.2 What to include
chunks.snippet: Describe what happened, approximate dates, relevant people, available records, and any immediate safety risk. Reports may be incomplete; do not delay a report while collecting evidence.

chunks.title: Workplace Conduct Policy
chunks.section: Workplace Conduct Policy > 3. Reporting concerns > 3.3 Immediate danger
chunks.snippet: For an imminent threat to physical safety, contact local emergency services first, then notify workplace leadership and People Operations when safe.

chunks.title: Workplace Conduct Policy
chunks.section: Workplace Conduct Policy > 3. Reporting concerns > 3.4 No retaliation
chunks.snippet: Northstar prohibits retaliation against anyone who makes a good-faith report, requests an accommodation, or participates in an investigation. Report suspected retaliation promptly even if the original allegation was not substantiated.

chunks.title: Workplace Conduct Policy
chunks.section: Workplace Conduct Policy > 4. Review and response > 4.1 Intake and triage
chunks.snippet: People Operations acknowledges reports when contact information is available, evaluates urgency, and assigns an impartial reviewer. A reported manager does not control the investigation.

chunks.title: Workplace Conduct Policy
chunks.section: Workplace Conduct Policy > 4. Review and response > 4.2 Confidentiality limits
chunks.snippet: Information is shared only with those who need it to assess and address the concern, but absolute confidentiality cannot be guaranteed. Investigators may need to interview witnesses and preserve records.

chunks.title: Workplace Conduct Policy
chunks.section: Workplace Conduct Policy > 4. Review and response > 4.3 Fair process
chunks.snippet: Northstar seeks relevant evidence and gives involved parties an opportunity to respond as appropriate. Outcomes may include coaching, training, corrective action, or no finding; employment action follows law and company standards.

chunks.title: Workplace Conduct Policy
chunks.section: Workplace Conduct Policy > 4. Review and response > 4.4 Records and follow-up
chunks.snippet: Records are stored in restricted systems. The reporter may receive a general closure update, but privacy limits disclosure of another employee’s personnel action.

chunks.title: Workplace Conduct Policy
chunks.section: Workplace Conduct Policy > 5. Common questions > 5.1 Can I report my manager?
chunks.snippet: Yes. Contact People Operations or ethics@northstar.example directly; reporting does not require manager approval.

chunks.title: Workplace Conduct Policy
chunks.section: Workplace Conduct Policy > 5. Common questions > 5.2 What if a colleague makes an offensive joke?
chunks.snippet: You may ask them to stop if safe and comfortable, but you are not required to confront them before reporting.

chunks.title: Workplace Conduct Policy
chunks.section: Workplace Conduct Policy > 5. Common questions > 5.3 What if I fear retaliation?
chunks.snippet: State that concern in your report; People Operations will consider interim protections and monitor follow-up.

chunks.title: Workplace Conduct Policy
chunks.section: Workplace Conduct Policy > 5. Common questions > 5.4 Who owns this policy?
chunks.snippet: People Operations administers HR-007. Security manages data-security incidents under SEC-001; the two teams coordinate when a case overlaps.

chunks.title: Workplace Conduct Policy
chunks.section: Workplace Conduct Policy > 6. Document control
chunks.snippet: **Owner:** People Operations. **Effective:** January 1, 2026. **Version:** 1.0. **Status:** Active. **Related policies:** HR-001,  SEC-001,  HR-004. People Operations or the responsible policy owner resolves ambiguities; applicable law and governing plan documents prevail where required. Policy updates are published in the People Portal. For policy questions, use the contacts specified above or consult HR-001 Employee Handbook.

chunks.title: IT Support Procedures
chunks.section: IT Support Procedures
chunks.snippet:
**Northstar Technologies | Policy IT-002 | Version 1.0**

> **Fictional training document.** Northstar Technologies, its contacts, systems, and policies are invented for RAG demonstration. This document does not replace applicable law, plan documents, or written agreements.

chunks.title: IT Support Procedures
chunks.section: IT Support Procedures > 1. Support channels > 1.1 How to contact
chunks.snippet: Use the fictional IT Service Desk portal for standard requests or email helpdesk@northstar.example. Include your work contact, device asset tag if relevant, affected application, symptoms, start time, and business impact.

chunks.title: IT Support Procedures
chunks.section: IT Support Procedures > 1. Support channels > 1.2 Priority levels
chunks.snippet: **P1 critical:** broad production or security-impacting outage; **P2 high:** major team disruption; **P3 normal:** individual impairment with workaround; **P4 low:** routine request or how-to question. IT determines final priority.

chunks.title: IT Support Procedures
chunks.section: IT Support Procedures > 1. Support channels > 1.3 Service targets
chunks.snippet: IT aims to acknowledge P1 incidents within 15 minutes during monitored coverage, P2 within 1 business hour, P3 within 1 business day, and P4 within 2 business days. These are fictional targets, not guarantees of resolution.

chunks.title: IT Support Procedures
chunks.section: IT Support Procedures > 2. Access and account recovery > 2.1 Password reset
chunks.snippet: Use approved self-service recovery when available. If locked out, contact IT Service Desk; staff verify identity through approved methods before resetting access. Never send passwords or one-time codes to support agents.

chunks.title: IT Support Procedures
chunks.section: IT Support Procedures > 2. Access and account recovery > 2.2 MFA recovery
chunks.snippet: Report lost authenticators or unexpected prompts immediately. IT verifies identity and re-enrolls MFA through an approved workflow; Security reviews suspicious activity under SEC-001.

chunks.title: IT Support Procedures
chunks.section: IT Support Procedures > 2. Access and account recovery > 2.3 New access
chunks.snippet: Managers submit access requests stating role, application, and business need. Application owners approve privileged access where required. IT cannot grant access solely because a colleague asks in chat.

chunks.title: IT Support Procedures
chunks.section: IT Support Procedures > 2. Access and account recovery > 2.4 Offboarding
chunks.snippet: People Operations triggers the approved separation workflow; IT disables access and coordinates equipment recovery under IT-001. Employees should not self-transfer accounts.

chunks.title: IT Support Procedures
chunks.section: IT Support Procedures > 3. Device and connectivity issues > 3.1 Troubleshooting steps
chunks.snippet: Record the error, time, and steps to reproduce. Restart only when safe, check approved status notices, and avoid changing security settings. Attach screenshots without exposing passwords or sensitive customer data.

chunks.title: IT Support Procedures
chunks.section: IT Support Procedures > 3. Device and connectivity issues > 3.2 Lost or stolen device
chunks.snippet: Immediately notify IT and security@northstar.example. Provide asset tag, last known location, and circumstances. IT coordinates containment and replacement; do not wait for a routine ticket response.

chunks.title: IT Support Procedures
chunks.section: IT Support Procedures > 3. Device and connectivity issues > 3.3 Remote connectivity
chunks.snippet: If VPN or internet access fails, notify your manager about work impact and open an IT ticket. Use a managed loaner or approved alternative; do not use a household computer to bypass restrictions.

chunks.title: IT Support Procedures
chunks.section: IT Support Procedures > 3. Device and connectivity issues > 3.4 Hardware repair
chunks.snippet: IT decides whether to repair, replace, or loan equipment. Do not send company devices to a third-party repair shop without authorization.

chunks.title: IT Support Procedures
chunks.section: IT Support Procedures > 4. Outages and escalation > 4.1 Major outage
chunks.snippet: IT posts verified updates in the approved status channel when available. Employees should not repeatedly retry sensitive operations or promise customers restoration times without confirmed guidance.

chunks.title: IT Support Procedures
chunks.section: IT Support Procedures > 4. Outages and escalation > 4.2 Security escalation
chunks.snippet: Phishing, suspected malware, mistaken data disclosures, and unexpected MFA requests are security incidents. Report immediately to security@northstar.example or IT; SEC-001 governs incident response.

chunks.title: IT Support Procedures
chunks.section: IT Support Procedures > 4. Outages and escalation > 4.3 Ticket follow-up
chunks.snippet: Reply to the existing ticket with new information rather than opening duplicates. Escalate a business-critical blocker to your manager and IT Service Desk, citing the ticket ID.

chunks.title: IT Support Procedures
chunks.section: IT Support Procedures > 4. Outages and escalation > 4.4 Examples
chunks.snippet: **I cannot log in on day one:** follow HR-005 and request verified account recovery. **My monitor broke:** open an IT-001 equipment ticket. **I clicked a phishing link:** report immediately to Security even if nothing appears to have happened.
